title: The future
intro: The future in `-jAk` is one of the easiest forms in Turkmen to build, and one of the easiest to get wrong. It never changes for the person: *Men geljek*, *Sen geljek*, *Olar geljek*. So the subject must always be said. This unit adds the negative with *däl* (*geljek däl*), questions (*geljekmi?*), and the time words for plans: *ertir*, *birigün*, *geljek hepde*, *indiki ýyl*, *iki günden soň*.

blocks.text: For what will happen, add `-jAk` to the stem: *-jak* after a back vowel, *-jek* after a front one. *gel-* → *geljek*, *oka-* → *okajak*. That is the whole form: `-jAk` takes **no personal ending**, so the same word serves every person.

rows.en: he, she or it will come
he, she or it will read

blocks.text: **So say who.** In the present and the past the ending tells you who: *gelýärin*, *geldim*. In the future nothing does, so the subject has to be there: *Men geljek*, I'll come; *Merdan geljek*, Merdan will come. On its own, *Geljek* doesn't say who is coming.

`-jAk` starts with a consonant, so stems keep their shape: the *t*-verbs keep *t* (*gitjek*, *etjek*, *aýtjak*), a stem's final *e* stays *e* (*işlejek*), and a vowel stem just adds the suffix (*okajak*, *ýaşajak*).
`-jAk` is the future you have decided on or are sure of: *Men ertir Mara gitjek*, I'll go to Mary tomorrow, I'm going to go. It covers both English **will** and **be going to**.

items.en: I'm going to read a book.
Aýna will stay at a hotel.

blocks.title: No ending, but a subject
blocks.text: Don't add an ending: `geljekin` and `geljekdim` are not the future. And don't drop the subject: for **I'll come tomorrow**, say *Men ertir geljek*, not just `Ertir geljek`. Questions need it too: *Sen haçan geljek?*, when will you come?

sections.title: Won't, will you? Negative and questions

blocks.text: For **won't**, put *däl* after the future, as a separate word: *Men geljek däl*, I won't come. You will also see the negative built with *-mA* before `-jAk`: *gelmejek*. Both are correct; this course writes *geljek däl*.

rows.en: he, she or it won't come

blocks.text: **Questions.** Write `-mY` onto the future: *Sen geljekmi?*, will you come? *-mi* after a front vowel, *-my* after a back one: *Ol okajakmy?* For **won't you?**, the particle goes on *däl*: *Sen geljek dälmi?*

rows.en: Will he, she or it come?
Won't he, she or it come?

items.en: Won't she come to see us?
No, we won't. (No, we won't go.)

blocks.text: **Short answers** repeat the verb, with the subject: *Sen geljekmi? — Hawa, men geljek* or *Ýok, men geljek däl*.

blocks.title: The particle on däl
blocks.text: In a negative question the particle goes on *däl*, the last word: *geljek dälmi?*, not `geljekmi däl`. And it is written attached: *geljekmi*, not `geljek mi`.

sections.title: Tomorrow, next week, in two days

blocks.text: These words point to the future. Like all time words, they usually come early in the sentence, before or after the subject: *Men ertir geljek* or *Ertir men geljek*.

blocks.caption: Future time words
head: Turkmen
Meaning
rows: in two days, two days later

blocks.text: *geljek* is also an adjective, **coming**: *geljek hepde*, literally **the coming week**. *indiki* means **next**: *indiki hepde*, *indiki ýyl*. Both are used and mean the same here.

For **in** a length of time from now, put the time in the ablative and add *soň*: *iki günden soň*, in two days; *bir hepdeden soň*, in a week. Compare **ago** in [A2 unit 1](a2-u01), where the time takes no ending: *iki gün öň*. On its own, *soň* means **later**: *Men soň jaň etjek*, I'll call later.

**Plans.** The present `-ýAr` also talks about what is arranged for soon ([A1 unit 6](a1-u06)): *Ertir Mara gidýärin*, I'm going to Mary tomorrow. `-jAk` says what you intend or are sure will happen: *Ertir men Mara gitjek*. For plans either is fine; for **will**, use `-jAk`.

items.en: The day after tomorrow we'll go to Ashgabat.
Next year they'll live in Dashoguz.

blocks.title: I'm leaving, I'll leave
blocks.text: English uses **I'm leaving tomorrow** for a fixed plan and **I'll leave** or **I'm going to leave** for an intention. Turkmen is similar: *Ertir gidýärin* for the plan, *Men ertir gitjek* for what you have decided.

blocks.title: soň takes -dan
blocks.text: **In two days** is *iki günden soň*, with *-den* on *gün*; **two days ago** is *iki gün öň*, with no ending. And *geljek hepde* has no ending either: not `geljek hepdede`.

summary: The future is stem + `-jAk` (*-jak, -jek*), with no personal ending: *geljek, okajak, gitjek, işlejek*.
With no ending to tell who, the subject must be said: *Men ertir geljek*, *Sen ertir näme etjek?*
*ertir, birigün, geljek hepde, indiki ýyl*; **in** two days is *iki günden soň*.
For plans, `-ýAr` (*Ertir gidýärin*) or `-jAk` (*Men ertir gitjek*); for **will**, `-jAk`.
